newsitem.title: USA: FNMA and partner fund housing project.
newsitem.headline: FNMA and partner fund housing project.

text.p: The Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae or FNMA) and the Housing Authority of Gwinnett County have agreed to fund construction of 324 affordable apartment units in suburban Atlanta, according to a Fannie Mae statement.

The financing structure, which combines Fannie Mae's tax-exempt variable rate bond credit enhancement and new construction products, makes the apartments affordable for families earning no more than $31,260, or 60 percent of the Atlanta area median income, the statement said.

"The financing structure also resulted in lower financing costs for the Housing Authority of Gwinnett County, which issued the variable rate tax-exempt bonds ... that financed the property," the report said.
Washington Capital, a member of Fannie Mae's multi-family Delegated Underwriting and Servicing (DUS) team of lenders, executed the transaction, it said.
KeyCorp's Key Bank provided both the construction loan and bond credit enhancement during construction, according to the statement.
Fannie Mae said its credit enhancement product will offer a lower mortgage rate to borrowers who finance multifamily properties, using lower variable rate tax-exempt bonds, known as "floater bonds."
